items.text: How do I check the status of my transfer?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
The easiest way is to log into your Wise account, go to Home to see your activity list, and click on the transfer you want to track.

items.text: When will my money arrive?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
We give an estimated delivery time when you set up your transfer, but delays can happen at any stage. Your money is on its way to Wise, we're processing it, or it's with the recipient bank, which might take up to one working day to release.

items.text: Why does it say my transfer is complete when the money hasn't arrived?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark your transfer Complete once we've sent the money to the recipient's bank. The receiving bank might still be processing it, which can take up to one working day. Your recipient should check their bank statement for a transaction from Wise or our banking partners using the reference number provided.

items.text: Why is my transfer taking longer than the estimate?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Delays can happen if your bank takes time to send money, security checks are needed, weekends or holidays have passed, or there's a mistake in recipient details. Your recipient can ask their bank to check on the payment and share a transfer confirmation to help them.

items.text: What is a proof of payment?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

A proof of payment is a document showing you've sent money from your bank account. It could be a PDF of your bank statement, a screenshot from your online bank, or other file types less than 10MB and up to five files altogether. We might ask for it if your money hasn't reached us in the expected time frame or if we need to verify it came from an account in your name.

items.text: What's a banking partner reference number?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
For every transfer you send with Wise, we give you a transfer number to use if you need to get in touch with us. For some transfers, we also provide a banking partner reference number because we send your money through local banking partners. You should give this number to your recipient so they can see where the transfer is once it shows as completed on your Wise account. They will need to share it with their bank if they get in touch with them, as banks might call it something else depending on the country.

items.text: The app says due today but my sister hasn't got anything yet.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
If the app says your money is due today, it should have arrived already because some banks need hours to process transfers from us. Your sister can check her bank statement for a transaction from Wise or our partners using the reference number you provided. If she still sees nothing, ask her bank to speed up processing with a transfer receipt.

items.text: It's been stuck on 'your money's being processed' for three days.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
If your transfer has been on "Your money's being processed" for more than two working days, you should check with your bank to make sure they've sent the money to us.

items.text: My landlord says he can't see the payment but Wise shows it as done.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
Wise marks your transfer complete when we've sent the money to your recipient's bank, but their bank may still be processing it. Your landlord should check their bank statement for a transaction from Wise or our banking partners using the reference number provided. They might also need to ask their bank to speed up the process with a transfer receipt if they haven't received it yet.

items.text: How long does a Swift transfer take to get to you?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
A Swift transfer usually takes one to six working days to reach us.

items.text: You emailed asking me for proof I sent the money. What do I need to send?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

To get your proof of payment accepted, you must upload a high-quality screenshot or PDF of your bank statement showing your name, account number, Wise's details, and the amount sent. We cannot accept text copied from an email, photos of screens, or password-protected files.

items.text: What's a UTR number?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
A banking partner reference number is what some banks call a UTR number, like in India. You can give this number to your recipient so they can track where the transfer is once it shows as complete on your Wise account.

items.text: I sent it on Friday afternoon and it still hasn't landed.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
If your transfer was due today, it might not show until the next working day because banks don't process transfers on weekends.

items.text: I spelled the recipient's name slightly wrong, will the money still get there?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
Small typos like spelling John as Jon usually won't stop your money from arriving on time. However, for some currencies such as JPY, a typo can be an issue and might delay or return the payment. If something is wrong with an account number, your money could take longer to arrive or get returned to us.

items.text: Can a screenshot from my banking app count as proof?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Yes, a high-quality screenshot from your online banking can count as proof of payment. It must clearly show your name, account number, the date, amount, currency, and reference. We cannot accept screenshots copied into an email or photos of computer screens.

items.text: My recipient got less money than I sent, why?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Your recipient's bank may have converted the currency again if their account is in a different currency than what you sent. They might also receive a slightly different amount due to fees or processing by their bank.

items.text: Is there anything I can do to make it arrive faster?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

The quickest way is to give your recipient a transfer receipt so their bank can track the money. If you sent money using Wise Interest or Stocks, check if there are daily sending thresholds that might cause delays.

items.text: Why are you doing a security check on my transfer?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
We run extra checks to keep your money safe as a standard procedure for regulated financial institutions. If we need more information from you, like ID or proof of where the money came from, we'll send you an email explaining what we need. We can't speed up these checks, but we work as fast as we can.
